bullets.title: MRVL surges 33% as Jensen Huang calls it potential 'next trillion-dollar company' at Computex
bullets.body: Marvell shares closed at a record $290.79, up nearly a third in one session, after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang publicly touted Marvell as a potential next trillion-dollar company during an onstage appearance with Marvell CEO Matt Murphy at Computex Taiwan. Multiple fintwit accounts flag this as a watershed moment analogous to Jensen's earlier call on NBIS. Speculation also emerged around potential MRVL inclusion in the S&P 500, with ALAB and CRDO also named as candidates.

bullets.title: NVDA Vera CPU and Computex keynotes signal coordinated AI infrastructure buildout
bullets.body: At Computex Taiwan 2026, NVIDIA announced the Vera CPU claiming 80% faster agentic task completion vs x86, framing it as the CPU of the AI factory era backed by $20B+ standalone revenue visibility with Oracle providing demand validation. Fintwit analysts noted NVDA, INTC, MRVL, and ARM keynotes functioned as a coordinated AI infrastructure roadmap reset, with AMKR named in Vera supply chain.

bullets.title: NVDA x MSFT deepen agentic AI partnership; MSFT adds more DC capacity in 18 months than Azure's first decade
bullets.body: At Microsoft Build 2026, NVIDIA and Microsoft unveiled an end-to-end agentic AI stack spanning Windows PCs (RTX Spark), cloud, and local infrastructure. Microsoft announced it added more data center capacity in the last 18 months than during Azure's entire first decade, previewed the Cobalt 200 chip, launched Majorana 2 quantum chip, and released seven new MAI models including AION reasoning. DGX Station systems with GB300 chips are shipping to developers with Dell and Supermicro as OEM partners.

bullets.title: AVGO +4.7% ahead of Q1 earnings; seen as big winner in custom AI chip demand alongside MRVL
bullets.body: Broadcom shares rose 4.7% on Tuesday and an additional 2.1% after-hours ahead of its Q1 earnings report. Multiple fintwit accounts position MRVL and AVGO as the primary beneficiaries of Wall Street's intensifying focus on custom AI silicon, with Marvell CEO also making the copper-to-optical interconnect case at Computex—stating 200G is the last generation where copper works.

bullets.title: WSTS raises 2026 semiconductor market forecast to $1.51T (+90%); memory segment seen +250%
bullets.body: The World Semiconductor Trade Statistics body raised its 2026 global semiconductor market forecast to $1.51 trillion from $975 billion, implying 90% growth. Memory is the standout segment expected to surge 250% YoY to exceed $800 billion. Americas forecast is +112%; 2027 market projected at $1.91T (+27%). One fintwit account notes semis are now trading 73% above their 200-day moving average—the widest premium since the Dot Com Bubble.

bullets.title: S&P 500 on historic 9-day, 9-week winning streak; 24 all-time highs in 2026
bullets.body: The S&P 500 closed at 7,612.12 on June 2, its sixth consecutive all-time high and ninth consecutive day of gains—one of the longest streaks in history. Options traders hit most bullish positioning in 10+ years with put/call ratio at 0.58. However, fintwit's SpotGamma notes the market is heavily long calls with minimal downside hedges, warning that a transition in positioning 'could be violent' should Iran tensions escalate further.

bullets.title: Ayar Labs joins NVIDIA NVLink Fusion; SIVE positioned as laser supplier to CPO ecosystem
bullets.body: Ayar Labs announced joining the NVIDIA NVLink Fusion ecosystem, adding to existing members Marvell Celestial and Lightmatter. A concentrated fintwit thesis argues that Sivers Semiconductors (SIVE) is the confirmed laser supplier to Ayar Labs and high-confidence supplier to Marvell and Lightmatter, with all three using GlobalFoundries germanium-free substrate where SIVE is the reference laser. EU Chips Act 2.0 launched June 3 with SIVE and NOK named as industry contributors alongside ASML and NXP.

bullets.title: Corning (GLW) +13% on Wiwynn CPO supply chain disclosure
bullets.body: After Wiwynn disclosed its CPO supply chain, Corning surged 13% with multiple other Taiwan-listed CPO suppliers (FOCI, Browave, Shunsin) hitting 10%+ circuit breakers. Fintwit sees this as an early read-through to optical interconnect demand ahead of broader CPO adoption.

bullets.title: PANW Q3 beats on EPS and revenue; BTIG raises PT to $333, TD Cowen to $330
bullets.body: Palo Alto Networks reported Q3 FY26 adj. EPS of $0.85 vs $0.79 estimate and revenue of $3.00B vs $2.94B estimate. Next-Gen Security ARR guided $8.90-8.95B; Q4 revenue guided $3.35-3.36B above the $3.27B consensus. Multiple analysts raised price targets; BTIG lifted PT to $333 from $268 and TD Cowen to $330 from $255, with the stock up 13% in extended trading. Fintwit reads PANW results as a second-derivative confirmation of AI data-center buildout strength across ANET, NVDA, AVGO, MRVL.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley initiates META as top pick with $775 PT (~30% upside)
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley initiated coverage on Meta with a top pick designation and $775 price target, implying approximately 30% upside. Thesis centers on Meta AI search, business/consumer subscriptions, core advertising upside, and Neocloud potential—each expected to add $1-3 to 2028 EPS with multiple expansion.

bullets.title: PLTR: Trump Truth Social post and FY26 guidance raise; analyst highlights 71% revenue growth
bullets.body: In April Trump directly named $PLTR in a Truth Social post praising Palantir's warfighting capabilities. In May, Palantir raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $7.65-$7.66B (+71% YoY) with US commercial guidance raised to +120% growth. Analyst consensus 2026 EPS sits around $1.46 with average PT ~$190 and some targets as high as $255. Despite the catalysts, the stock has barely moved in the two months since the Trump post.

bullets.title: MSFT leading hybrid AI monetization; GOOGL and MSFT flagged as making right moves in AI arms race
bullets.body: Multiple fintwit accounts flag Microsoft as entering the next phase of AI monetization via its developer ecosystem, noting Azure Arc and Edge AI as hybrid AI enablers. MSFT and GOOGL are described as 'making the right moves' in the AI arms race. Hybrid cloud inference margins are noted as minimum 80%, supporting the economic case for sustained investment.

bullets.title: INTC: 14A process moving forward de facto; 18A ramped to high volume at Computex
bullets.body: Fintwit notes Intel's 18A process node has ramped to high volume on multiple products and 14A is on track, though Intel is unlikely to provide an official confirmation announcement. Intel appeared prominently at Computex with CEO on stage, viewed as signaling PE/enterprise capital commitment to AI data center buildout. Analyst describes INTC's AI infrastructure turnaround story as 'more credible' but execution-dependent.

bullets.title: China's NAND market share now rivals Micron and SanDisk; competitive pressure rising
bullets.body: Multiple fintwit accounts flag a report showing China has achieved NAND market share comparable to Micron and SanDisk, raising competitive concerns for legacy NAND players. Separately, NAND supply is forecast to grow at 22% CAGR with Kioxia signaling supply discipline through 2029.

bullets.title: ChatGPT hits 1B monthly active users; Goldman CEO warns markets in 'greed' mode
bullets.body: ChatGPT reached 1 billion monthly active users. Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon separately described markets as being in 'greed mode' and characterized inflation as a higher near-term priority than employment. Bain research also published findings showing actual corporate AI cost-savings are falling well below initial projections, raising questions about enterprise AI ROI timelines.

bullets.title: Oil nears $95/bbl on stalled US-Iran talks; Gulf tensions put/call ratio near 10-year low
bullets.body: Brent crude settled at $96/bbl (+1.07%) and WTI at $93.76/bbl (+1.74%) on a third consecutive day of gains as US-Iran peace talks stalled and Iran's IRGC claimed retaliatory missile/drone strikes on US bases in Kuwait and UAE. TD Securities sees Brent averaging $104 in H2 with upside risk to $150+. Fintwit's SpotGamma separately warns markets are positioned heavily long calls with put/call OI near 10-year lows.

bullets.title: Gold overtakes US Treasuries as world's second-largest reserve asset
bullets.body: Multiple fintwit sources note gold has surpassed US Treasuries to become the world's second-largest central bank reserve asset. JGB yields continue rising across the curve (10Y at 2.64%, 20Y at 3.535%, 40Y at 3.765%), adding to global duration pressure.

bullets.title: NVDA Vera CPU supply chain: ORCL provides demand validation; AMKR in supply chain
bullets.body: A detailed fintwit thread notes Oracle is providing demand validation for NVIDIA's Vera CPU with $20B standalone revenue visibility. Amkor Technology (AMKR) is identified as being in the Vera CPU supply chain. The MGX platform supporting Vera includes 80+ partners across systems, power, and cooling.

bullets.title: BRUN: $471M take-or-pay with Mira Murati's Thinking Machines; one of few neoclouds with NVDA Exemplar status
bullets.body: Fintwit flags BRUN as recently IPO'd with a $471M take-or-pay agreement with Thinking Machines (Mira Murati's AI lab) and NVDA Exemplar status—one of very few neoclouds to hold this designation. Author expects BRUN to appear on Leopold Aschenbrenner's 13F and values it at approximately half of NBIS's valuation.

bullets.title: LITE flagged with 'Die Hard' conviction; COHR part of NVDA's own CPO program
bullets.body: One fintwit account posts a high-conviction bullish call on Lumentum (LITE) with a 'Die Hard' designation. Separately, a detailed CPO ecosystem thread notes LITE and COHR are part of NVIDIA's own CPO/NVLink program distinct from the SIVE-supplied ecosystem partners, with Celestial and Lightmatter expected to multi-source but SIVE preferred for gen-1.
